h: Every Jewish Soul Will Bear the Fruit of Torah

p: and the tree of the field shall give its fruit" (Vayikra 26:4).
This too is hard to understand in its plain sense:
what kind of promised reward is this
for one who merits to be
for whom a kav of carobs is enough
from Erev Shabbos to Erev Shabbos?
It may be that this too
(זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בְּהַר, חֵלֶק ג קי, ב)
the land of HaKadosh Baruch Hu
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא פִּנְחָס, חֵלֶק ג רמג, ב)
we call it Torah she'b'al peh.
is along the lines of what is stated
'It is a tree of life, etc.' (Mishlei 3:18)"
אֵין עֵץ אֶלָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
"'Tree' means nothing other than HaKadosh Baruch Hu;
כִּי הָאָדָם עֵץ הַשָּׂדֶה (דְּבָרִים כ, יט)
'for man is the tree of the field' (Devarim 20:19);
this is the tree of the field
And this is what it says,
"And the tree of the field shall give its fruit";
and these are the very words
which are destined to bear fruit.
And so too what is expounded (in Toras Kohanim):
What kind of blessing is this?
even what one brings to it
does not count as a blessing.
In the simple sense one can say
that it will bear fruit immediately,
And the inner intent one may say
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, ג)
"Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest,
so is my beloved among the sons";
and nevertheless they expounded from it
that Yisrael are compared to an apple tree
are the nations of the world,
who are compared to barren trees.
And this is "the field" — the well-known field,
שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כז, כז)
this is a field of apples;
and in the language of the holy Zohar,
for so it is expounded from this pasuk
that the fragrance of Gan Eden entered with him;
And there is the dwelling of the souls of Yisrael;
and "the Tree of Life in the midst of the garden"
and the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil,
impure and pure, kosher and unfit
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קיא, א)
(as stated in Ra'aya Mehemna, Zohar III 111a).
And this is what it says
as a promise for the future:
and the tree of the field shall give its fruit":
that there will be no barren trees
which are words of Torah and its chiddushim,
which are the fruits of the land
as it says in the Navi (Yirmiyahu 31:33):
for they shall all know, etc."
For this is the purpose of the exiles:
and all the souls of Yisrael
And on Shabbos is the time to merit
as stated in the holy Zohar
this is Torah she'b'al peh, etc.";
for Shabbos is the middah of Malchus;
and especially at the third meal,
"You are One and Your Name is One, etc."
